text:
elaine: FYI, getting multiple customer reports of 500s + timeouts to hosted inference endpoints since 09:10 UTC. Support ticket INC-9384, customer acct-4932. I see the inference-runner containers on a subset of GPU nodes restarting in a loop.

mike: Can you paste the node/container logs? Any obvious OOMs or segfaults?

elaine: Pasted from one node (shortened):
```
Mar 15 09:11:58 runner[pid=4281]: allocating KV cache...
Mar 15 09:12:01 runner[pid=4281]: error: cuda runtime error (2) out of memory
Mar 15 09:12:01 runner[pid=4281]: terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
Mar 15 09:12:01 kernel: [12345.678] Killed process 4281 (runner) total-vm:123456K, anon-rss:110000K, file-rss:0K
Mar 15 09:12:02 kubelet: Back-off restarting failed container
Mar 15 09:12:03 runner[pid=4302]: Segmentation fault (core dumped)
```

sophie: That looks like a mixed OOM then SIGSEGV during the restart. Could be an allocator/driver race when the runtime tries to recover. Which model/profile were they hitting?

elaine: Customer calls v2-large-quantized with batch_size=8 and max_tokens=1024. Traffic spike around 09:09.

raj: Batch 8 on quantized model -> on some GPUs quantization kernels use more temporary memory. We've seen this on older drivers. Which driver/kernel?

elaine: Nvidia driver 525.85, CUDA 11.7, runtime build 2026.02. Logs show a few low-level nvml OOM reports before the process exits.

mike: Quick mitigations:
- scale down max_batch to 1 on the hosted pool via routing policy
- apply temporary rate-limiting for that model to affected tenants
- re-route heavy customers to CPU-fallback or smaller model variant

anne: Support applied rate-limit and made a routing change for acct-4932. Customer still seeing ~30% error rate but reduced.

deploy-bot: [09:18] Rollout: applied config override to hosted-pool model:v2-large-quantized -> max_batch=1 (by anne) :white_check_mark:

raj: Can we reproduce? I'll try a local repro on dev-gpu-3 with the same driver and quantized kernels. Need exact payload pattern.

elaine: Repro steps from the customer's replay:
1) 8 concurrent requests, each with 1024 max_tokens, prompt length ~350 tokens
2) streaming enabled, client keeps connection open
3) short inter-request spacing (bursting)

sophie: I can repro a single OOM locally by simulating 6 concurrent requests. When the runner tries to prefetch KV for long context, memory spikes, then the allocator fails and we see SIGSEGV on next start.

mike: Notes from quick triage:
- root cause likely kernel-level memory spike in quantized attention kernels under concurrent prefetch + batching.
- older driver + certain cuda allocator path triggers unrecoverable state on process exit -> segfault on restart.

raj: Short-term fix ideas:
- force max_batch=1 for that model across hosted-pool for next 6 hours
- pin model to a different quantization variant (lower workspace)
- update driver on a canary pool to 535.x and test

elaine: We applied max_batch=1 and did a small routing split. Error rate dropped from ~60% -> ~8% for the impacted customer. Still seeing occasional restarts on a small subset of nodes.

anne: Support has informed the customer and created SR-6914 with status "mitigated". They requested ETA for full fix.

mike: Long-term: eng-runtime to add explicit allocator guard for quantized kernels, detect pre-OOM and refuse heavy prefetch, and treat segfault path as flaky driver state -> avoid immediate restart, drain node first. I'll open an RFC.

sophie: I've got an experimental patch that reduces KV prefetch concurrency; it passed load smoke on dev-gpu-3. I'll stage it to canary 2 nodes.

deploy-bot: [09:56] Canary rollout started: runtime.patch/kv-prefetch-throttle -> canary-nodes (2/2) :rocket:

elaine: After canary rollout we still saw one node restart at 10:02 but overall client 500s dropped to <2% across hosted.

raj: Action items:
- mike: lead postmortem + RFC for allocator guard (owner)
- sophie: follow-up on patch and full rollout plan (owner)
- infra: schedule driver upgrade canary and run longer stress tests (assigned)
- support/anne: keep customer updated, offer credits if SLA breached

mike: I'll file the incident and assign to eng-runtime. Ticket: INCIDENT-2026-0315-01. Postmortem target 72h.

anne: Customer notified. They asked for a timeline; gave rough ETA ~48-72h pending driver testing.

elaine: Thanks team. I'll keep this thread updated with logs and the postmortem link. :thumbsup:
